findings.title: Failed/stale keyspace takes node pools down instead of warning
findings.claim: use_keyspace sets current_keyspace before knowing whether USE succeeded and never rolls it back (also affects cluster/worker.rs for new nodes), so a failed USE now drops the connection instead of joining the pool with a warning as before; after a typo'd keyspace or a keyspace dropped server-side, refill connections keep failing USE and the pool ends up Broken(UseKeyspaceError), causing nodes to be reported down and even fully-qualified queries to fail after churn or a rolling restart.

findings.title: Discard path for a full shard leaks the connection count metric
findings.claim: When a shard-aware connection lands on a shard that is already full, the connection is dropped without calling dec_total_connections even though the count was already raised in start_opening_connection (:1051), so total_connections drifts upward, especially behind NAT.

findings.title: Metrics-fix commits are undocumented in the PR description
findings.claim: About half the diff (commits de164845, 0d91aa54, 617139df), including three new tests, fixes a different bug (metrics on pool clear, excess-pool clear and reshard), but the PR description, its Fixes line, and the "logically coherent" checkbox only cover the keyspace fix.

findings.title: Validation command omits --features metrics, skipping metrics assertions
findings.claim: The checklist's listed validation command does not include --features metrics, which is not a default feature, so it skips the metrics tests and the get_total_connections assertions in the keyspace tests.

findings.title: Checklist claim that commit messages explain what/why is inaccurate
findings.claim: All four commits have a subject line only, with no body, contradicting the checklist claim that commit messages explain what and why.

findings.title: Test name overstates coverage of refill/backoff behavior
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill only checks need_filling() and never drives run(), so it doesn't actually show that a refill or backoff happens.

findings.title: Keyspace switch during in-flight USE wastes a connection instead of retrying
findings.claim: If the user switches keyspace while USE old_ks is running and it fails, the connection is thrown away and backoff grows, instead of being retried with the new keyspace.

findings.title: USE failure downgraded from warn! to debug-level logging
findings.claim: The failure is now logged only at debug instead of warn! as before, so a misconfigured keyspace no longer shows up at default log levels.

findings.title: many_connections test fails, but same failure exists on main
findings.claim: Running cargo test -p scylla --lib --features metrics network::connection_pool gave 8 of 9 passing; the one failure, many_connections, needs a live Scylla node and fails the same way on main.

findings.title: Metrics test uses a polling sleep loop instead of a deterministic wait
findings.claim: The metrics test uses a 1 ms sleep loop inside a 5 s timeout; it isn't flaky, but paused time or a notification would make it deterministic.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops single decrements instead of a batch helper
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections in a loop; a single decrement-by-N helper would be simpler.
